newsitem.title: UK: UK sets 1.3 billion stg PFI hospital programme.
newsitem.headline: UK sets 1.3 billion stg PFI hospital programme.

text.p: Junior health minister Alan Milburn on Thursday gave the go-ahead for a 1.3 billion stg hospital building programme, which he said was the largest in the history of the National Health Service.
The programme will go ahead under the Private Finance Initiative (PFI) following a review of major hospital construction contracts in the NHS.

New hospital building contracts will be signed in North Durham, South Buckinghamshire, Calderdale, Carlisle, Hereford, Wellhouse, Worcester, Bishop Auckland, South Manchester, South Tees, Swindon and Bromley.
Two more hospitals, one in Norwich and one in Gravesham, had already signed binding commercial contracts.
The hospitals were chosen after a review of the PFI and local health service needs.
Milburn told a news conference: "Today the government is announcing the largest new hospital building programme in the history of the NHS, worth about 1.3 billion.
"Yesterday the government invested an extra 1.2 billion stg in the NHS for patient care. An extra 2.5 billion for the NHS is about putting the people's priorities first."
